run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:43:38Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert reflects real failing requests at frontend-proxy: its 'ingress' spans carry error=true / http.status_code 504 and its error share was ~0.97% of its span rate at 01:43:38 (annotation: 1.0888). Sampled traces show a consistent chain: the load-generator's user_add_to_cart / user_view_cart requests end in 15s 504s at frontend-proxy; frontend's /api/cart handlers hit gRPC errors from cart ('9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage ... Wasn't able to connect to redis'), and cart's own server spans for AddItem/GetCart error after ~476-480s with 'System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()'. The cart pod logged 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 01:41:40Z followed by repeated 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' until at least 01:50:14Z, i.e. before the alert fired. However I could not identify what broke cart's Redis connectivity: the valkey-cart pod stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, no OOM/failcnt, memory far under its 10Mi limit, and the otel-collector redis receiver kept reporting redis values through 01:51:00. The only fault-injection setting in scope, flagd's cartFailure flag ('Fail cart service'), is 'off' in the flagd-config ConfigMap, but cart evaluates flags from flagd:8013 at runtime and flagd's effective in-pod flag state could not be observed, so an injected cart-failure remains an unverified hypothesis, not a supported cause. cart's CFS throttling rose to 0.73-0.97 of periods only after 01:46, so it is more plausibly a consequence than the trigger. No root cause object is named.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error signal comes from span_name 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR (0.0895/s over 10m at 01:43:38); span_name 'router frontend egress' had 0 error rate. At 01:43:38 frontend-proxy ERROR spans were 0.1778/s against 18.17/s UNSET spans, i.e. an error share of 0.969% (alert annotation says 1.0888).

frontend-proxy's 5m error rate was ~0 through 01:40:38, first rose at 01:44:38 (0.567/s), stayed ~1.31-1.45/s from 01:46:38 to 01:50:38 and was 0 by 01:56:38; its non-error span rate fell from ~19-21/s to ~8.7/s during the same interval. Over the same hour the only services with sustained nonzero error rates were frontend-proxy, frontend, cart and (small) checkout.

Sampled traces show frontend-proxy ingress spans of ~15.000s ending in 504 whose child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true with http.status_code 0, with the corresponding frontend GET/POST spans lasting ~15.0s; e.g. trace 6386302d4551ec2a0e0d33dd2d212f24 contains frontend-proxy ingress 15.000543s/504 and a child frontend POST span of 15.000530s with http.status_code 200.

frontend's error spans in the window are cart operations: grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 0.0579/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.0386/s, POST /api/cart 0.0579/s, GET /api/cart 0.0386/s, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 0.10/s, with rpc.grpc.status_code=9 and message '9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis'.

cart's own server spans are the failing dependency side: POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (2 spans, 476.5-477.9s) and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (1 span, 479.7s) carry error=true plus otel.status_description 'Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() in .../ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 97 at ...GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync ...')' with Grpc.Core.RpcException.

cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logged 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 2026-11-18T01:41:40.940Z, then 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' repeatedly from 01:43:57.139Z through at least 01:50:14.241Z (68 matching lines, recurring every few seconds).

cart's error-span rate first became nonzero at 01:46:00 (0.129/s, 2m rate) and frontend's at 01:45:00 (0.111/s); both were declining by 01:53:00 (cart 0.170/s, frontend 0.510/s) and frontend-proxy's error rate was 0 in the 5m window ending 01:56:38.

cart's pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 was Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-18T01:10:26Z on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae; its init container wait-for-valkey-cart terminated Completed with exitCode 0 at 01:10:36Z. The cart containers run with limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi and env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013.

valkey-cart pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr was Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 01:10:35Z on the same node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, with an empty lastState; its container_memory_failcnt stayed 0 for every sample up to 01:55:38 and container_memory_max_usage_bytes peaked at 5,693,440 bytes against a 10Mi limit (deployment limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi).

The otel-collector redis receiver series for this redis (otel_scope .../receiver/redisreceiver) kept returning values while cart was failing: redis_memory_used_bytes is present with the identical value 1,710,360 bytes from 01:42:00 through the last returned sample at 01:51:00, and rate(redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="user"}) fell from ~0.0015 to ~0.0003 at 01:45:38 and 0 at 01:48:38. An instant query of redis_memory_used_bytes at 01:56:00 returned no series.

cart container's CFS throttled-period ratio was ~0.14-0.29 through 01:44:00 and then jumped to 0.834 (01:46:00), 0.735, 0.841 and 0.972 (01:52:00), i.e. after the first logged redis connection failure at 01:41:40Z.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's demo.flagd.json defines cartFailure ('Fail cart service', state ENABLED) with defaultVariant "off", and every other flag in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) also has defaultVariant "off"; the flagd Deployment (revision 2) mounts this ConfigMap at /config-ro and its init-config container copies demo.flagd.json into an emptyDir at /etc/flagd, which flagd and flagd-ui share.

No cart or valkey-cart workload rollout occurred in this window: their ReplicaSets cart-755465879b and valkey-cart-58df56c79c have creationTimestamp 2026-11-18T01:10:26Z with the same images (demo:2.1.3-cart, valkey:8.1.3-alpine); the only newer ReplicaSet is flagd-75c6477d68 (01:12:12Z), with the older flagd-c47676d99 at 0 replicas.

Events in namespace otel-demo reference a Pod named cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s that is absent from the current pod list: reason Killing (count 75, last 2026-11-18T01:46:28Z) and FailedKillPod (count 30, last 01:46:27Z, message 'error killing pod: ... KillContainerError: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded ...'). cAdvisor still reports that pod's container at 0 CPU with a constant 29,138,944-byte working set.

Checked and healthy in the same failing traces: product-catalog's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct spans returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in 93-129 microseconds, and frontend's GET /api/products/{productId} spans returned http.status_code 200 in 1.3-5.7 ms; frontend's GET/POST spans that took 15s still reported 200 at the frontend server, so the failure is in the cart path, not the product path.

valkey-cart shows no container-level failure signature: restartCount 0, empty lastState (no terminated instance), memory failcnt 0 across the window, max usage 5.69MB vs its 10Mi limit, and Ready=True since 01:10:37Z - so an OOMKill/crash of the redis container is not supported by the evidence.

The fault-injection setting that matches this symptom, flagd's cartFailure ('Fail cart service'), reads defaultVariant "off" in the flagd-config ConfigMap; no other fault/delay/failure flag in that file is set to anything but off, so the ConfigMap does not show an active injection.

Mechanism hypothesis (well supported by the chain): cart lost its Redis connection at 01:41:40Z and could not re-establish it, so its AddItem/GetCart handlers blocked for ~476-480s and returned FAILED_PRECONDITION; frontend's /api/cart calls then exceeded frontend-proxy's ~15s deadline, producing the 504 ingress errors that fired the alert.

Alternative hypothesis (unverified): cart's runtime feature-flag evaluation against flagd (FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013) returned cartFailure='on' during 01:41-01:54, which would produce exactly these 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' errors while valkey-cart stays healthy and idle; flagd's effective in-pod flag file (a copy in an emptyDir that flagd-ui can mutate) could not be read, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Contributing-factor hypothesis: cart runs at a 45m CPU limit and its CFS throttled-period ratio rose to 0.73-0.97 from 01:46 onward, which may have starved StackExchange.Redis reconnect attempts and lengthened the outage; the throttle jump starts after the first connection failure at 01:41:40Z, so it is more likely a consequence of the retry storm than its trigger.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself broke. Its error 504s are 'ingress' spans whose child 'router frontend egress' spans call frontend and the upstream frontend spans lasted the full ~15s, while frontend's own failures are cart RPC failures - the proxy is where the deadline surfaces, not where the fault originates.

Advisory: read flagd's effective runtime flags (flagd-ui / flagd HTTP API at flagd:8013 and the /etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json copy in the flagd pod) to see whether cartFailure was toggled around 01:41-01:54, and capture flagd logs; compare against the flagd-config ConfigMap, which currently shows it off.

Advisory: verify cart-to-valkey connectivity independently (e.g. a TCP/TLS connect and PING from the cart pod to valkey-cart:6379, plus Cilium/hubble flow logs for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr) and raise cart's 45m CPU / valkey's 10m CPU limits, which are far below what a throttling ratio of up to 0.97 implies is needed.

gaps: The cause of cart's loss of Redis connectivity at 01:41:40Z is not identified: no network-layer evidence was available and a cluster-wide NetworkPolicy query returned nothing (an empty result only shows this query matched no objects; it is not proof that no policy existed then).

flagd's effective runtime flag values are unverified: the flagd pod's logs returned no lines, Prometheus has no flagd/feature-flag metric series, and flagd reads a copy of demo.flagd.json from an emptyDir created at 01:12:12Z that flagd-ui can mutate, so the ConfigMap read now is not proof of the in-pod file at 01:41-01:54; the change_history integration is not available to show who changed anything.

valkey side evidence is missing: the valkey-cart container log stream returned no lines, and there is no metric for redis client connections, blocked clients or rejected connections, so whether redis refused/could not accept connections cannot be checked.
The redis receiver series end after the 01:51:00 sample and an instant query at 01:56:00 returned no data, so whether valkey remained scrapeable until the errors stopped (~01:54) is unknown.

Kubernetes events cover only 2026-11-17T01:59:42Z onward and only the currently retained set; events that could explain a change at 01:41:40Z may have expired, and the event for Pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (FailedKillPod, last 01:46:27Z) cannot be tied to the cart/valkey connectivity failure, nor can its node be determined from the available metrics.

checkout's error-rate series rose to 0.0259-0.0444/s between 01:48:38 and 01:52:38, but a trace search for checkout error spans in 01:44-01:56 returned no traces, so checkout's failures are not tied to the cart cause by evidence and its own reason is unknown.

No node-level CPU/memory/network metrics or node logs were available, so node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (which hosts both cart and valkey-cart) could not be examined for a local networking fault; the node objects' conditions are the state at query time only.
next_steps: Inspect flagd's runtime flag state (flagd-ui/API and the /etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json copy inside the flagd pod) for cartFailure around 01:41-01:54 and correlate with the cart log line 'Connection failed. Disposing the object' at 01:41:40Z.
Run an independent connectivity check from the cart pod to valkey-cart:6379 (TCP connect and PING) and review Cilium/hubble flows for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr during 01:41-01:55.
Review Redis INFO client/error counters on valkey-cart to rule out client-limit or blocked-client conditions that would not appear in the six available redis_* series.
Reconsider cart (cpu 45m) and valkey-cart (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) resource limits, which are tight relative to the observed throttling, once the trigger is identified.
